## Coordinating action
Request, propose and negotiate shared or individual action.
Boundary: Require a successful request, proposal, commitment or response about action. Merely describing a desire or future event is insufficient.

Assess requests, offers, suggestions, undertakings, acceptance or refusal and changes to plans. 옮겨 주세요 asks help with moving something; 도와드릴까요 offers the speaker’s help, and 같이 쉴까요 proposes shared action in context. 제가 가져올게요 can undertake responsibility with a listener-oriented intention, whereas a prediction in 을 거예요 need not promise. 좋아요 after a concrete invitation can accept contextually; elsewhere it may just evaluate an object. 오늘은 어려워요 can decline a proposed activity indirectly when the difficulty is clear. 토요일은 어때요 adjusts timing in response to a Friday conflict. An isolated copied 주세요 without an object or recoverable request is absent. A question about capability is not automatically a request. Honorific and speech-level choices should fit the relationship, but do not require maximal formality in ordinary conversation or explicit pronouns when the participants are clear.

## Feelings and viewpoints
Express internal states, evaluations and positions.
Boundary: Require a correctly expressed feeling, desire, preference or position. An ordinary factual assertion is not automatically an opinion.

Evaluate desire, preference, emotion, judgment and agreement. 배우고 싶어요 expresses the speaker’s desire to learn; 싶다 behaves as a descriptive predicate rather than an action verb. 좋아해요 can take a liked object, while 좋아요 describes something as pleasing or good with a different construction. 저는 커피가 좋아해요, intended as an ordinary transitive liking statement without another correct use, mismatches the object construction. Do not erase a separate correctly expressed preference. 기뻐요 expresses happiness; 좋다고 생각해요 frames a judgment. 저도 그렇게 생각해요 aligns with an identifiable viewpoint, while 알겠어요 can simply acknowledge comprehension. 차요 can select a preferred drink contextually when that choice is being asked, but naming a drink in a list does not establish liking. Recover omitted experiencers from context; third-person feelings may require reporting or appropriate evidence rather than indiscriminate reuse of first-person self-report patterns.

## Information exchange
Seek, supply and verify information relevant to the exchange.
Boundary: Require successful information seeking or a relevant informative response. Question-shaped requests for action do not qualify just for their form.

Assess unknown-information questions, responsive answers, confirmation and useful detail. 가게가 몇 시에 닫아요? asks for closing time without English subject-verb inversion. 다섯 시에요 can supply the time contextually. 다섯 시에 닫죠? checks a proposition, but 지요 has other uses and is not automatically a question about truth. A polite 줄 수 있어요? request may primarily seek action rather than information about capability. A copied 어디 from a word list without a recoverable question is absent. A relative description such as 창문 옆에 있는 helps select a needed object; extra length alone does not establish useful detail. 뭐라고 하셨어요? after unclear speech repairs hearing rather than verifies an understood fact. Question force can be conveyed by context and intonation with ordinary 요 endings; do not require 까 for every question or an explicit second-person pronoun.

## Managing conversation
Establish contact, coordinate turns and repair mutual understanding.
Boundary: Require a successful opening, response, turn/topic action or repair. Sending any message or quoting a greeting does not automatically qualify.

Recognize greetings, leave-taking, acknowledgment, clarification, reformulation, correction and floor or topic management. 안녕히 가세요 addresses a departing person, while 안녕히 계세요 addresses someone staying; choose according to the encounter. 알겠어요 can acknowledge understanding, not necessarily future knowledge or agreement. 다시 말씀해 주세요 seeks repetition after trouble hearing or understanding. 다시 말하면 introduces another formulation only if it clarifies identifiable prior content. 금요일이 아니라 토요일이었어요 can repair a misheard day. 다른 이야기를 해도 될까요? seeks a topic transition, whereas every sent message is not automatically turn management. Quoting a greeting as vocabulary or copying a transition ending alone is absent. Short responses with 요 can be complete social acts. Distinguish acknowledgment from agreeing with a position or accepting a task using the preceding exchange, and preserve appropriate register instead of judging every conversation against formal written style.

## People, things, and places
Establish referents and describe properties, locations, quantities and relationships.
Boundary: Require an identifiable referent and a correctly expressed property, spatial relation, quantity or relationship. Naming alone does not demonstrate every function in this group.

Identify nominal descriptions, qualities, location or movement, possession or relationships, and quantity or comparison. 이분은 제 동료예요 identifies a person; 방이 넓어요 predicates a descriptive verb without adding English be. 에 with 있어요 locates something; 에서 normally locates an activity rather than static existence. 제 contracts 저의 and can identify possession. 책 두 권 counts books with a counter; 2번 as a route label does not count two objects. 보다 with 더 can compare properties. A copied particle 의 with no recoverable relationship is absent. 책상 위에요 can answer a where-question contextually. Subjects and some particles may be omitted in appropriate conversation, so do not require full written-style repetition. 방이 넓다예요, intended as an ordinary descriptive predicate and standing alone, incorrectly combines predicate endings. Register and honorific choices are part of the construction; polite 요 does not itself demonstrate a spatial or descriptive function.

## Possibilities and constraints
Express capability, permission, requirements and epistemic limits.
Boundary: Distinguish ability, permission, obligation and likelihood. Similar wording can serve a request instead; judge the actual function.

Recognize ability, allowance, requirements, possible outcomes and confidence. 고칠 수 있어요 expresses ability or practical possibility; 고쳐도 돼요 can grant permission. 해야 해요 states a requirement, 안 해도 돼요 removes it, and 하면 안 돼요 prohibits an action. 비가 올 수도 있어요 presents possible rain rather than learned skill. 확실하지 않아요 limits confidence. A factual unqualified rain report does not automatically demonstrate possibility. A copied 수 without an identifiable predicate is absent. 네 after a permission question can grant permission contextually if spoken by the appropriate person. An indirect request using 수 있어요 need not assert physical ability. Where correct wording supports capacity or practical opportunity, uncertainty between those subfunctions does not itself make group use unclear. Preserve the difference between 안 for negation and 못 for inability where relevant, and accept suitable everyday contractions rather than imposing a formal written ending.

## Reasons and connections
Relate propositions through explanation, consequence, condition, contrast and support.
Boundary: Require a correctly expressed relationship between ideas. Sequence alone is not causation, a condition or an argument.

Judge causal, consequential, conditional, contrastive and evidential links. 아서 or 어서 can give a reason, but also connects actions in other ways; 올라가서 may mean going up and then doing something rather than because of going up. 그래서 commonly introduces a consequence. 비가 오면 expresses a rain condition; no future suffix is required inside it merely because the event is anticipated. 지만 can contrast two properties. 소리가 들려서 links audible evidence to an inference when the following clause states that inference. A copied 그래서 with no identifiable prior circumstance or result is absent. 피곤해서요 can answer a why-question contextually without a repeated main clause. 고 may simply list or order events, not claim causation. A reason for acting and evidence supporting belief are distinct functions. Judge the clause relation actually expressed, and do not award this group merely because two unrelated sentences occur together.

## Time and events
Locate events in time and express their temporal structure.
Boundary: One correctly expressed temporal relationship is sufficient. Present properties alone do not establish temporal skill. Judge meaning in context, not a tense label.

Look for temporal reference, duration or recurrence, sequence and event phase. 지금 라디오를 고치고 있어요 presents an ongoing repair; a suitable simple present can describe a routine. 어제 고쳤어요 locates a repair earlier. 내일 갈 거예요 anticipates a later event, while 겠 can express intention, inference or conventional acknowledgment and is not automatically future timing. 매주 marks recurrence and 두 시간 동안 duration. 먼저 and 그다음 order actions; 다 읽었어요 explicitly presents a completed reading. An isolated copied 어제 without an event or contextual answer is absent. 어제 저녁에 can answer a question about when an identified action happened. A current quality such as 방이 넓어요 does not automatically demonstrate temporal skill. Do not demand an English progressive or perfect counterpart in every translation, and distinguish an appropriate shorter conversational predicate from a genuinely broken tense or aspect construction.
